integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] An original expressive 3D CG animated Brazilian street-news comedy at a peaceful protest by adult PC gamers. A small asynchronous adult crowd stands behind them in a warm Brazilian square. Soft afternoon sunlight from screen-left, colorful matte clothes, coherent contact shadows. Plain red-brick storefront and plain navy awning. No existing character, real person, store name or numerical price claim. No violence, fire, weapons or damage.
Exactly TWO enormous plain pale ivory BLANK paper protest boards high above every head, fully front-facing, rectangular and nearly still. Left paper stays within x28to356, right within x412to740. Both boards lie above y480, with a generous air gap between the paper and all hair, hands, microphones and bodies. Both boards and all four corners stay fully visible for the entire shot. Separate supporters hold the wooden poles far below the papers. No occlusion and no board bouncing during laughter or chanting. Exactly two boards, no other signs. All paper surfaces have absolutely no letters, numbers, symbols, drawings or texture marks. Exact huge lettering will be composited later. Leave the upper navy awning plain without writing. Static eye-level medium-wide waist-up portrait interview. Exactly two enormous matte ivory blank rectangular protest placards, one left and one right, remain fully visible above every head throughout. Each board occupies almost half the768pixel picture width. All four real paper corners visible, with no overlap between the boards. Paper between y130 and y590, all heads and hair below y650. Supporters hold separate wooden poles far below the papers. The paper boards remain nearly motionless as people react. A flat terracotta brick wall and plain navy awning behind the papers; no windows, shop lettering, white rectangles, extra placards, logos or symbols. Warm afternoon light. Fixed framing supports exact later typography and the faces reacting to the punchline. No camera movement, cut or zoom.

A different original fictional adult pair. Reporter screen-left: adult woman with medium olive skin, chin-length copper bob and tan blazer over a dark blouse. Gamer screen-right: adult man with warm brown skin, wavy black hair, rectangular black glasses and a rust-colored hoodie. Distinct adult supporters with different clothes and faces. No continuing person or prop transfers between the independent interviews.

No actual monitor, computer, box, budget document, money, wallet or phone. Empty hands. Gamer gives one tiny matter-of-fact shrug on meu orçamento; shoulders then settle. Solid planted support, no collapse, physical injury or violent act. Reporter holds a plain unbranded microphone.

He is proud that his fictional monitor has no defective pixel. Say Veio with bright confidence, then shift to dignified deadpan and land orçamento as the absurd financial victim. This is a harmless budget metaphor, never physical death or violence. Reporter listens with closed lips until orçamento, looks once from his shrug back to his eyes, recognizes the wordplay, fails to hold a smile and gives an audible short belly laugh with two uneven shoulder movements. He reacts to her loss of composure and joins later with a smaller voiced laugh. Supporters laugh at separate later moments, recover, then chant once; the two leads smile silently during the chant.

ACTING SCORE: Play the ridiculous answer as a sincere attempt to convince the reporter. Start with engaged curiosity and attentive listening, not constant grinning. One dominant meaningful gesture accompanies the answer. The reporter perceives the punchline only after its final word, glances briefly toward the relevant prop, then tries to suppress a smile and fails. The laugh is clearly visible and AUDIBLE: microphone lowers to waist, eyes squeeze, head tips back briefly, then a small forward lean with two uneven shoulder bounces and one hand against the abdomen. The gamer holds a straight face for a short recognition beat, then cracks into an amused grin and joins with a shorter irregular voiced laugh. Nearby supporters react later and differently; no synchronized mechanical swaying. Both catch their breath and exchange an amused look. Laughter must have a cause in this exchange. Keep feet planted, prop supported and boards motionless. No frozen faces, talking-mouth-only acting, anticipation before the joke, flat monotone or tiny polite chuckle.

Exactly THREE verbal turns in native Brazilian Portuguese. Reporter(S1), an adult female voice, asks once at 0.2 to 2.4 seconds, curious and attentive: <d>[Portuguese] Esse monitor veio sem pixel morto?</d> Reporter then listens with closed lips. Gamer(S2), an adult male voice, answers once at 2.8 to 7.5 seconds, with clear ordinary conversational Brazilian Portuguese diction, mock seriousness and a brief pause between sentences: <d>[Portuguese] Veio! Quem morreu foi o meu orçamento!</d> No repeated words or additional utterances. Reporter reacts only after the last word, with a short recognition beat, an unsuccessful attempt to hold a smile, microphone lowered below the mouth, then a clear AUDIBLE warm voiced belly laugh. Eyes close, shoulders bounce twice unevenly, body leans forward briefly and recovers. Gamer joins later with a shorter clearly audible spontaneous laugh. The crowd reacts after the two leads, with different timing, never synchronized swaying. Laughing is nonverbal: no invented words, babble or extra syllables. Let laughter resolve by 10.1 seconds. At 10.5 to 13.5 seconds the adult supporters chant ONCE: <d>[Portuguese] Mais tela, menos parcela!</d> The reporter and gamer are silent and smiling during the chant. Recover with an exchanged amused look from 13.5 to 15 seconds. No additional speech.

One static continuous shot, normal speed, no cuts or zoom. Only specified exact dialogue tags contain spoken words. Laughter is native in-scene nonverbal voiced laughter with irregular breaths, not extra syllables or words. No canned laugh track, narrator, music, subtitles, logos, watermarks or added verbal remarks. Keep background street ambience soft under dialogue and laughter.
